message.reasoning:
I need to decide on an auction bid for SHORT_LINE.

I have $546 cash and am the only active player left. The auction for SHORT_LINE is at $68, with a minimum next bid of $69. I plan to raise by $1 increments up to $99, since the mortgage value is $100. I will drop out if the bid reaches $100 or higher.

Folding now would gift p2 a $32 arbitrage profit. I will continue bidding up to $99 to limit their gain. Both players have most railroads mortgaged, so rent income is minimal.

Bidding $99 nets a net gain of $1 after mortgaging. At $100 the mortgage value equals the purchase price, so there is no arbitrage profit. I have enough cash to bid $69 immediately.

I considered jumping straight to $99 to end the auction quickly. Incremental bidding is better because it forces p2 to decide at each dollar and may make them drop out earlier. They have matched every bid so far, suggesting they are committed to matching. I am weighing whether they want to deny me the cash arbitrage or acquire the railroad for strategic reasons.
